attributes.body_ja:
「せい」は、悪（わる）い結果（けっか）を起（お）こした原因（げんいん）や理由（りゆう）を表（あらわ）す名詞（めいし）です。「(A) が原因（げんいん）で」や「(A) という理由（りゆう）で」という意味（いみ）で、その責任（せきにん）を誰（だれ）かや何（なに）かに向（む）けるときに使（つか）われます。「せいで」はひらがなで書（か）かれることがほとんどですが、漢字（かんじ）では「所為（せい）」と書（か）かれます。この漢字（かんじ）は、「所為（しょい）」と読（よ）むと「行（おこな）い」という意味（いみ）になります。このことから、「せいで」は「〜の行（おこな）いによって」という意味（いみ）から生（う）まれた使（つか）い方（かた）だと考（かんが）えると覚（おぼ）えやすいかもしれません。

「せい」は、連体形（れんたいけい）の語（ご）のあとに付（つ）けて使（つか）われます。格助詞（かくじょし）「で」と合（あ）わさった「せいで」の形（かたち）で、そのあとに悪（わる）い結果（けっか）の内容（ないよう）について説明（せつめい）することが多（おお）いです。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「所為（せい）」は、ある結果（けっか）になったことを、誰（だれ）かや何（なに）かの「行（おこな）い」が原因（げんいん）だと責（せ）めるような場面（ばめん）でよく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
Although written almost exclusively in hiragana, せい is a noun that may be better understood from its kanji, 所為（せい）, meaning 'doings'. せい is used to convey negative results that occurred due to the behavior or actions of another person/thing. Because of this, common translations of せい are 'fault', 'due to', or 'because of'.

As せい is a noun, it may be used after the attributive form of any other word. The case marking particle で will also regularly be seen after せい, especially when conveying the (B) result that occurred 'with' or 'by means of' those 'doings'.

Fun Fact

The 'doings' that 所為（せい） represents is similar to the negative 'doings' that is used in English to place blame. This can be seen in phrases such as 'it was the weather's doings', or 'ah, so the missing cookies were your doings!'

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: The difference between おかげで and せいで
Expressing that something is to blame or is the cause of

attributes.body: Both せいで and につき express cause, but with different nuance and tone. せいで is more colloquial and typically introduces a cause for a negative result, e.g. 雨のせいで試合が中止になった ('The game was canceled because of the rain.'). につき states a reason more neutrally and is often used in formal written announcements, e.g. 工事中につき通行止め ('Closed to traffic due to construction.').

second_relatable.title: につき
second_relatable.meaning: Due to, On account of, Each or every

attributes.body: ために and せいで can both mean 'due to (A)', but with a difference in tone. せいで almost always implies a negative or undesirable result. ために can be used with either positive or negative nuance. Also, ために can mean 'for the purpose of (A)', which せいで cannot.

first_relatable.title: ために
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, Because of, As a result of

attributes.body: Both mean 'because of', but with opposite tone. おかげで expresses a thankful cause, e.g. 先生のおかげで合格できた ('Thanks to my teacher, I passed.') せいで places blame for something negative, e.g. 雨のせいで試合が中止になった ('The game was canceled because of the rain.')

Both せいで and そのため(に) show cause and effect, but せいで follows a word or phrase and implies a negative result or blame, e.g. 台風のせいで試合が中止になった ('The game was canceled because of the typhoon'), while そのため(に) is used at the beginning of the sentence and neutrally shows a logical result of whatever was previously stated. そのため(に) can also express 'for the purpose of (A)', which is a nuance せいで cannot have.

second_relatable.title: そのため(に)
second_relatable.meaning: For that reason, Because of that, To that end
